question: Which contemporary chronicler acknowledged that Raziyya Sultan was more capable than her brothers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Minhaj-us-Siraj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Minhaj-us-Siraj was a 13th-century Persian historian and the author of Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, a general history of the Islamic world dedicated to Sultan Nasir-ud-din Mahmud.

• He was a contemporary of Raziyya Sultan (रजिया सुल्तान) and personally observed her reign; he acknowledged that she was more capable and qualified than her brothers, though he lamented that she was a woman.

• Raziyya (r. 1236–1240) was the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate and of Muslim India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tabaqat-i-Nasiri is a key primary source for the history of the Slave/Mamluk dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

• Raziyya was the daughter of Sultan Iltutmish, who nominated her as his successor over his sons.

• She was overthrown and killed in 1240 after conflict with the Turkish nobility (the Chahalgani/Forty).

NOTE

• Ziauddin Barani (Option 2): A 14th-century historian, author of Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi, who wrote during the reigns of the Tughlaq rulers, not Raziyya's time.

• Al-Biruni (Option 3): An 11th-century Persian scholar who came with Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote Kitab-ul-Hind (Tahqiq-i-Hind).

• Ibn Battuta (Option 4): A 14th-century Moroccan traveller who visited India during Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq's reign and wrote Rihla (Kitab-ul-Rihla).

question: Who were called 'Bandagan' in Persian in Delhi Sultanate?
option_4: Military slaves purchased by the Sultan
solution_text:
The correct answer is Military slaves purchased by the Sultan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The term Bandagan (बंदगान) in Persian referred to the special slaves purchased for military service by the Sultans of Delhi.

• These military slaves were carefully trained to man some of the most important political offices in the kingdom and were personally loyal to the Sultan.

• The Delhi Sultans, especially the Khaljis and Tughlaqs, appointed such slaves to high administrative and military posts because they depended entirely on their masters.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Since bandagan were dependent on their masters, Sultans could trust and rely upon them more than other nobles.

• The institution of slave-officers ensured centralised control over the administration.

• The Slave Dynasty (1206–1290) itself was founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, originally a slave of Muhammad Ghori.

NOTE

• Aristocrats and nobles (Option 1): The high-ranking hereditary elite; they were not the bandagan, who were purchased slaves.

• Landed chieftains appointed as governors (Option 2): Local landholders and iqta-holders, distinct from the personal military slaves.

• Religious scholars (Option 3): Known as the ulama, they dealt with religious and legal matters, not military slavery.

question: Which article of the Indian Constitution mentions that "There shall be a High Court for each State"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 214.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 214 (अनुच्छेद 214) of the Indian Constitution states that "There shall be a High Court for each State".

• The High Courts are dealt with in Part VI of the Constitution under Articles 214 to 231.

• Parliament can, however, establish a common High Court for two or more States or a State and a Union Territory (Article 231).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 215: High Court to be a court of record.

• Article 216: Constitution of High Courts (judges appointed by the President).

• Article 217: Appointment and conditions of the office of a Judge of a High Court.

NOTE

• Article 124 (Option 1): Deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court of India.

• Article 226 (Option 3): Empowers High Courts to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.

• Article 32 (Option 4): The right to constitutional remedies, empowering the Supreme Court to issue writs; called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

question: The first-ever batch of female cadets at the National Defence Academy graduated in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2025.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first-ever batch of female cadets at the National Defence Academy (राष्ट्रीय रक्षा अकादमी), Khadakwasla, Pune, graduated in 2025.

• Women were admitted to the NDA for the first time following a Supreme Court order, joining in 2022; after the three-year course they passed out in 2025.

• A total of 17 women cadets were part of this historic first batch that graduated with the 148th course.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The NDA is a tri-service academy training cadets of the Army, Navy and Air Force together before pre-commission training.

• The Supreme Court permitted women to appear for the NDA examination in August 2021.

• The NDA was established in 1954 and is located at Khadakwasla, Maharashtra.

NOTE

• 2021 (Option 1): The year the Supreme Court allowed women to appear for the NDA exam, not the graduation year.

• 2022 (Option 2): The year the first women cadets joined/were inducted into the NDA.

• 2023 (Option 3): An intermediate year of training for the first batch, not their passing-out year.

question: There are over ______ Lakh ODF Plus Villages in December 2024.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.61.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of December 2024, there were over 5.61 lakh ODF Plus villages in India under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen Phase II (स्वच्छ भारत मिशन-ग्रामीण).

• An ODF Plus village is one that has sustained its Open Defecation Free status and has arrangements for solid and/or liquid waste management.

• The goal of SBM-G Phase II is to make all villages ODF Plus.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2nd October 2014.

• SBM-Grameen is implemented by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti.

• ODF Plus villages are categorised as Aspiring, Rising, and Model based on waste-management arrangements.

NOTE

• 7.56 (Option 2): An incorrect higher figure not matching the December 2024 data.

• 4.21 (Option 3): An incorrect figure lower than the actual count of ODF Plus villages.

• 3.85 (Option 4): An incorrect and understated figure for ODF Plus villages.

question:
In the Union Budget 2025, which of the following has been announced for Gig Workers in India?
I. e-Shram registration
II. Healthcare security under PM Jan Arogya Yojana
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2025-26 (केंद्रीय बजट 2025), the government announced measures for gig and platform workers of online platforms.

• They will be provided identity cards and registration on the e-Shram portal, so both statements are correct.

• They will also get healthcare coverage under the PM Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The scheme is expected to benefit around 1 crore gig workers.

• e-Shram is the national database of unorganised workers, launched in 2021.

• PM Jan Arogya Yojana provides health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year under Ayushman Bharat.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as healthcare security under PM-JAY was also announced.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as e-Shram registration was also announced.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both benefits were announced in Budget 2025.

question: The term "MOVCDNER" which is seen in news in October 2024 is related to which sector?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agriculture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• MOVCDNER stands for Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region, which is related to the agriculture (कृषि) sector.

• It is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare to promote organic farming in the North Eastern states.

• The mission develops certified organic production in a value-chain mode, linking growers with consumers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• MOVCDNER was launched in 2015-16 and is a sub-mission under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture.

• The North Eastern Region has traditionally been organic by default, giving it a natural advantage.

• The scheme supports farmer producer organisations (FPOs), certification, and marketing.

NOTE

• Defence indigenous (Option 1): Related to self-reliance in defence manufacturing (Atmanirbhar Bharat in defence), not MOVCDNER.

• E-vehicles (Option 3): Concerns electric mobility schemes like FAME India, unrelated to MOVCDNER.

• Nuclear energy promotion (Option 4): Handled by the Department of Atomic Energy, not connected to this agriculture mission.

question: Which country topped the Environmental Performance Index 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Estonia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Estonia (एस्टोनिया) topped the Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2024.

• The EPI is released biennially by Yale University and Columbia University in collaboration with the World Economic Forum.

• It ranks countries on environmental health, ecosystem vitality, and climate change performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In EPI 2024, India was ranked near the bottom of the index (176th).

• The EPI uses over 50 performance indicators across multiple categories.

• The index helps policymakers identify environmental problems and track progress toward sustainability goals.

NOTE

• Germany (Option 2): A high-ranked European nation on the EPI but not at the top in 2024.

• Norway (Option 3): A strong environmental performer, yet not ranked first in EPI 2024.

• Switzerland (Option 4): Frequently among the leaders but did not top the 2024 index.

question: According to the Report of the Technical Group on Population Projections (July 2020), India's elderly population is expected to reach ______ million by 2031.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 193.4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Report of the Technical Group on Population Projections (July 2020), India's elderly population (बुजुर्ग आबादी) is projected to reach about 193.4 million by 2031.

• This represents a sharp rise of roughly 41% over the decade in the number of persons aged 60 years and above.

• The finding was highlighted in the India Ageing Report and related government data.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The elderly are expected to make up around 13.1% of the population by 2031.

• India's share of the elderly is projected to reach about 20% by 2050.

• The Technical Group functions under the National Commission on Population, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

NOTE

• 103.4 (Option 1): Close to the 2011 elderly population figure, not the 2031 projection.

• 91.4 (Option 2): An understated figure not matching the 2031 projection.

• 113.4 (Option 3): An incorrect intermediate figure lower than the projected 2031 total.

question: The 19th Asian Games were held in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 19th Asian Games (19वें एशियाई खेल) were held in 2023 at Hangzhou, China.

• Though originally scheduled for 2022, they were postponed to September–October 2023 due to the COVID-19 pandemic but retained the name 'Hangzhou 2022'.

• India won a record 107 medals (28 gold, 38 silver, 41 bronze) at these Games.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Asian Games are held every four years and are organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.

• The 20th Asian Games are scheduled to be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, in 2026.

NOTE

• 2019 (Option 1): No Asian Games were held in this year.

• 2020 (Option 2): No Asian Games were held in this year.

• 2024 (Option 4): The Summer Olympics (Paris) were held this year, not the Asian Games.

question: Volleyball was introduced in the Asian Games in ______ for Men.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1958.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Volleyball (वॉलीबॉल) was introduced in the Asian Games for men in 1958 at the Tokyo Asian Games.

• The 1958 Asian Games (3rd edition) were hosted by Tokyo, Japan.

• Volleyball has remained a regular team event in the Asian Games since then.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Volleyball was invented by William G. Morgan in 1895 in the USA.

• A standard volleyball team has six players on court.

• Volleyball made its Olympic debut at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

NOTE

• 1951 (Option 1): The year of the first Asian Games in New Delhi, but volleyball was not part of it.

• 1954 (Option 2): The year of the second Asian Games in Manila, without men's volleyball.

• 1982 (Option 4): The year of the Asian Games in New Delhi, long after volleyball was introduced.

question: What is the newly revised official length (in km) of India's coastline?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11098.8.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The newly revised official length of India's coastline (भारत की तटरेखा) is 11,098.8 km.

• This is a significant increase from the earlier figure of 7,516.6 km, following a re-measurement using modern methods that account for the intricate, tidal and meandering nature of the coast.

• The revision was based on measurement at a finer scale considering estuaries, creeks, and bays.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states.

• India's coastline touches 9 coastal states and several Union Territories.

• The earlier length of 7,516.6 km included the mainland and island territories.

NOTE

• 7516 (Option 1): The old/previous official coastline length before the revision.

• 13065.6 (Option 3): An incorrect overstated figure not matching the revised length.

• 15035.5 (Option 4): An incorrect and exaggerated figure for India's coastline.

question: Who is the author of the book 'The White Tiger'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aravind Adiga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The White Tiger (द व्हाइट टाइगर) was written by Aravind Adiga.

• The novel won the prestigious Man Booker Prize in 2008, Adiga's debut novel.

• It tells the story of Balram Halwai, a village boy who rises to become a successful entrepreneur, exploring themes of class struggle in modern India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The novel was adapted into a Netflix film in 2021.

• Aravind Adiga's other works include Last Man in Tower and Between the Assassinations.

• The Man Booker Prize is awarded for the best original novel written in English.

NOTE

• Vikram Seth (Option 1): Author of A Suitable Boy and The Golden Gate.

• Amitav Ghosh (Option 3): Author of The Shadow Lines, The Glass Palace, and the Ibis trilogy; first English author to win the Jnanpith Award.

• Rohinton Mistry (Option 4): Author of A Fine Balance and Such a Long Journey.

question: Which art form developed as a result of the fusion of Greek and Indian artistic styles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhara art.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gandhara art (गांधार कला) developed as a result of the fusion of Greek (Hellenistic) and Indian artistic styles.

• It is also known as the Graeco-Buddhist or Indo-Greek school of art and flourished mainly under the Kushana ruler Kanishka.

• Its subject matter was chiefly Buddhist, but the technique and style were Greek, showing Buddha with wavy hair, muscular body, and drapery.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Gandhara school flourished in the north-western region around modern Peshawar and Taxila.

• Grey sandstone and stucco were commonly used materials.

• It was one of the first schools to make images of the Buddha in human form.

NOTE

• Mathura art (Option 1): An indigenous Indian school that developed at Mathura using red sandstone, without foreign influence.

• Amaravati sculpture (Option 2): A school that developed on the banks of the Krishna river in South India, patronised by the Satavahanas.

• Gupta art (Option 4): The classical Indian art of the Gupta period, marked by refinement and spirituality, as at Sarnath.

question: The below given image is of which of the following planet of our solar system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saturn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The image shows Saturn (शनि), easily identified by its prominent and spectacular ring system.

• Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second-largest planet in the solar system after Jupiter.

• It is a gas giant composed mainly of hydrogen and helium.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Saturn has the most extensive ring system, made mostly of ice particles with rocky debris.

• Saturn has the largest number of moons; its largest moon is Titan.

• It is the least dense planet, being less dense than water.

NOTE

• Mars (Option 2): The 'Red Planet', fourth from the Sun, known for its reddish appearance due to iron oxide.

• Mercury (Option 3): The smallest planet and closest to the Sun, with no ring system.

• Venus (Option 4): The hottest planet and Earth's 'twin' in size, without any rings.

question: A girl with 50 kg mass climbs up a rope through a height of 5 metres. She takes 25 s to accomplish the task. What is the power (in watts) expended by the girl?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 98.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Power (शक्ति) is the rate of doing work: Power = Work done / Time taken.

• Work done = mgh = 50 kg × 9.8 m/s² × 5 m = 2450 J (taking g = 9.8 m/s²).

• Power = 2450 J / 25 s = 98 watts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SI unit of power is the watt (W); 1 W = 1 joule/second.

• 1 horsepower (hp) = 746 watts.

• The SI unit of work and energy is the joule (J).

NOTE

• 49 (Option 1): Obtained by wrongly halving the correct value or using an incorrect time/height.

• 68.6 (Option 3): Results from an incorrect calculation not matching mgh/t with the given data.

• 88.2 (Option 4): An incorrect value not consistent with the given mass, height, and time.

question: In May 2025, scientists have created the first 'pangenome' of which crop, an important staple food in Asia?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2025, scientists created the first 'pangenome' of rice (चावल), a key staple food crop across Asia.

• A pangenome is a complete map of the genetic material of many varieties of a species, capturing genes that a single reference genome would miss.

• This helps breeders develop improved, high-yielding and climate-resilient rice varieties.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rice is the staple food for more than half of the world's population.

• China and India are the largest producers of rice in the world.

• The scientific name of rice is Oryza sativa.

NOTE

• Maize (Option 2): An important cereal (Zea mays), but not the crop for which this pangenome was created.

• Barley (Option 3): A cereal grain (Hordeum vulgare) used for food, animal feed and brewing.

• Wheat (Option 4): A major staple cereal (Triticum), but not the crop referred to in this news.

question: Which one of the following was the only Rajput state that defied Mughal power?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mewar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mewar (मेवाड़) was the only Rajput state that persistently defied Mughal power for a long time.

• Its ruler Maharana Pratap famously resisted Akbar and fought the Battle of Haldighati (1576) rather than submit.

• Unlike other Rajput states, Mewar refused matrimonial alliances and long resisted Mughal supremacy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mewar finally reached a peace treaty with the Mughals under Rana Amar Singh I and Emperor Jahangir in 1615.

• The capital of Mewar was Chittor, later shifted to Udaipur.

• The rulers of Mewar belonged to the Sisodia clan of Rajputs.

NOTE

• Amber (Option 2): The Kachhwaha state whose ruler Raja Bharmal was among the first to ally with Akbar through matrimony.

• Bikaner (Option 3): A Rathore Rajput state that entered into an alliance and served the Mughals.

• Marwar (Option 4): The Jodhpur state whose rulers largely cooperated with and served the Mughal empire.

question: As of July 2025, the Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited holds which of the following CPSE status?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Miniratna-I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of July 2025, Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (भारत संचार निगम लिमिटेड) holds the status of a Miniratna Category-I CPSE.

• Miniratna Category-I status is granted to profit-making CPSEs that meet certain financial criteria, giving them greater operational and financial autonomy.

• BSNL is a state-owned telecommunications company under the Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• CPSEs are classified as Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna (Category-I and II) based on financial performance and autonomy.

• Miniratna Category-I CPSEs can incur capital expenditure without government approval up to prescribed limits.

• BSNL was incorporated in 2000.

NOTE

• Maharatna (Option 1): The highest category granted to very large, globally competitive CPSEs like ONGC, NTPC and SAIL.

• Navratna (Option 2): A category above Miniratna, granting greater autonomy to strong-performing CPSEs.

• Miniratna-II (Option 4): A lower sub-category of Miniratna with fewer financial powers than Category-I.

question: Who was the chairman of the Tax Reforms Committee 1991?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja J. Chelliah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Raja J. Chelliah (राजा जे. चेलैया) was the chairman of the Tax Reforms Committee, 1991.

• He is often called the 'Father of tax reforms in India' for his contribution to restructuring the country's tax system.

• The committee recommended lowering and rationalising tax rates and broadening the tax base.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The committee was set up in the context of the 1991 economic reforms/liberalisation.

• Its recommendations shaped both direct and indirect tax reforms in the 1990s.

• Chelliah also founded the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP).

NOTE

• Manmohan Singh (Option 1): The Finance Minister during the 1991 reforms and later Prime Minister of India, but not the committee's chairman.

• P. Chidambaram (Option 2): A former Finance Minister of India, known for the 'dream budget' of 1997.

• Shakti Kant Das (Option 4): A former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and ex-Finance Secretary.

question:
In the context of Budget, which of the following statement is correct regarding capital expenditure?
I. It does not creates physical or financial assets.
II. Acquisition of machinery is an example of capital expenditure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Capital expenditure (पूंजीगत व्यय) is the expenditure that either creates assets or reduces liabilities of the government.

• Statement I is incorrect: capital expenditure does create physical or financial assets, so the statement claiming it does not is wrong.

• Statement II is correct: acquisition of machinery (or land, buildings, equipment) is a classic example of capital expenditure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Examples of capital expenditure include construction of roads, buildings, purchase of machinery, and loans to states.

• Revenue expenditure, by contrast, neither creates assets nor reduces liabilities (e.g., salaries, subsidies, interest payments).

• The Budget is divided into a Revenue Budget and a Capital Budget.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement I wrongly denies that capital expenditure creates assets.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, because Statement I is false.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because Statement II is true.

question: At which of the following places Mangal Pandey was hanged till death for attacking his officers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barrackpore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mangal Pandey (मंगल पांडे) was hanged till death at Barrackpore (in present-day West Bengal) on 8 April 1857.

• He was a sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry who attacked his British officers, sparking the Revolt of 1857.

• His act of rebellion at Barrackpore is regarded as one of the first sparks of the First War of Indian Independence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The immediate cause of the revolt was the greased cartridges of the new Enfield rifle, rumoured to contain cow and pig fat.

• The Revolt of 1857 began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

• Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed the symbolic leader of the revolt.

NOTE

• Chandigarh (Option 1): A modern planned city and Union Territory, not connected with Mangal Pandey's execution.

• Delhi (Option 3): The centre of the 1857 revolt under Bahadur Shah Zafar, but not the place of Mangal Pandey's hanging.

• Lucknow (Option 4): A major centre of the 1857 revolt associated with Begum Hazrat Mahal, not Mangal Pandey's execution.

question: A majority of the total membership of the House and a majority of not less than ______ of the members present and voting is required for adoption of effective clauses and motions for consideration and passing of Constitution Amendment Bills.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2/3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Constitution Amendment Bill requires a majority of the total membership of the House and a majority of not less than two-thirds (2/3) (दो-तिहाई) of the members present and voting.

• This special majority is prescribed under Article 368 of the Constitution.

• Certain amendments additionally require ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 368 deals with the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure.

• A Constitution Amendment Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament.

• There is no provision for a joint sitting for passing a Constitution Amendment Bill.

NOTE

• 3/4 (Option 1): Not the majority prescribed for Constitution Amendment Bills.

• 4/5 (Option 3): Not a majority requirement mentioned in the amendment procedure.

• 5/6 (Option 4): Not the fraction required for passing Constitution Amendment Bills.

question: The decades ______ are referred to as the period of steady population growth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1921-1951.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The decades 1921–1951 are referred to as the period of steady population growth (स्थिर जनसंख्या वृद्धि) in India.

• The year 1921 is called the 'Year of the Great Divide', after which India's population began to grow steadily.

• During this phase both birth rate and death rate were high, and growth was moderate and steady due to improvements in health and stability.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The period 1901–1921 is called the period of stagnant/stationary population growth.

• 1951 onwards (1951–1981) is known as the period of population explosion/rapid high growth.

• India conducts its census every ten years; the first complete census was in 1881.

NOTE

• 1921-1941 (Option 2): An incorrect span that omits the 1941–1951 decade of the steady-growth phase.

• 1911-1931 (Option 3): Overlaps with the stagnant phase (1901–1921) and is not the steady-growth period.

• 1931-1981 (Option 4): Extends into the population-explosion phase after 1951.

question: Which of the following is an approximate year (in BCE) of birth of Gautama Buddha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 560.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The approximate year of birth of Gautama Buddha (गौतम बुद्ध) is around 560 BCE (commonly cited as c. 563 BCE).

• He was born as Siddhartha at Lumbini (in present-day Nepal) into the Shakya clan.

• He attained enlightenment (Nirvana) at Bodh Gaya and became the founder of Buddhism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Buddha delivered his first sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana) at Sarnath.

• He attained Mahaparinirvana (death) at Kushinagar around 483 BCE.

• His teachings centre on the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.

NOTE

• 432 (Option 2): Not associated with the birth year of Gautama Buddha.

• 361 (Option 3): Not related to the traditional date of Buddha's birth.

• 263 (Option 4): Closer to the era of Ashoka's reign, not Buddha's birth.
